content.comment_body: Hello! As someone new here and not much of a programmer, I'd appreciate any help. The attached program runs properly on [product_name] with [version_no], but the analog input seems to behave like a digital input. The device is a [product_name], [article_no]. Inputs 1 and 2 come from an incremental encoder, inputs 3 and 4 are min and max sensors, and input 7 is a 0–10 Vdc potentiometer. Outputs 1–4 control a motor direction (CW/CCW) based on the potentiometer. Apologies for the long story—hope it’s clear, and thank you in advance.
Please upload the [document] diagram as a ZIP file. Thanks.
The program has been uploaded as a ZIP file.

I’ve attached a screen video. I downloaded the program, rearranged the blocks for better visibility, set the hardware selection to [product_name] [version_no], and transferred the program to my device. In the video you can see that AI1 (terminal I7) works as expected, but I can't comment on the rest of the program since I don’t have the required hardware.

Hello [user_name], I observe the same behavior on both versions: on [version_no], the connected motor turns fully CW or CCW depending on the voltage at IN7 (around 1.5V triggers mode switching). On the earlier model, the motor responds proportionally (e.g., half way at 5V, three-quarters at 7.5V) as intended.

I can't give a detailed answer since I don’t know the system, circuit function, wiring, or peripheral signals. I can say that with a 0–10 V input and gain of 0.4, you get 400 units in [product_name], meaning a resolution of 0.025V per unit. So 1.5V at the analog input equals 60 units (1.5V / 0.025V = 60). That’s the comparator threshold set for B003. I can't say where the difference is between [article_no] hardware versions without more information.
Thanks for your help. I'll continue searching.
It may help to organize your program and add clearer comments and names for better understanding. This will assist both you and others in troubleshooting faults. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], thanks for watching! As I mentioned, I'm not formally trained in programming, so I simply loaded and used the program on [version_no]. Since they're difficult to source now, we've switched to [version_no] and encountered the issue. The uploaded program is original—hope that helps.

I recognize the main portion of the program from a German conference ([document], pages 1 and 2). It's very time-sensitive and may not work on every controller. You could try changing I1/I2 to I5/I6 and test it on [product_name], but it's unclear if that would solve the issue. The block order is also important here; this is a complex program from the author. Alternatively, you can search for encoder solutions in other conference materials or continue using [product_name] as long as possible. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to transition a motor control program between hardware versions of [product_name] and encountering issues with the analog input on newer platforms. On more recent devices, the analog input behaves as a digital signal, causing the motor logic to switch fully rather than provide proportional control as on earlier models. Participants suggest revising the program structure and documentation to clarify logic and aid troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent analog signal handling and proportional motor control across product generations of [product_name] without having to modify their program. They are seeking reliable hardware and software compatibility for analog inputs.
